activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Line

feedback.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{2}t+1 \\ y=5-\frac{1}{2}t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}t+1 \\ 5-\frac{1}{2}t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}t \\ -\frac{1}{2}t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(1,5,\frac{1}{3})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
